sections.h2: Which office mails the tax statement for a house in Galveston?
sections.html:
The Galveston County Tax Office bills and collects for the City of Galveston, for Galveston ISD, for Galveston College and for the county itself, so most island owners get a single statement that covers several taxing units. Every dollar on it goes to a local unit rather than to the state.

Two offices matter. The Galveston Central Appraisal District appraises every parcel at its January 1 market value and rules on exemption claims. Its customer service desk takes mail at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, Texas 77591, and call (409) 935-1980. The tax office collects the money, accepts mail at 722 21st Street, Galveston, TX 77550, and answers questions about balances at (409) 766-2481.

The county tax office says only the appraisal district can change ownership or mailing address on a parcel. The tax office will pass a correction along as a courtesy, but a seller who moved or a buyer who just closed should file the change with the appraisal district so the next statement reaches the right person.

sections.h2: What rate did Galveston's council adopt for 2026?
sections.html:
The city adopted a 2026 rate of $0.416273 per $100 of property value when City Council approved the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. The city's news release describes that figure as the no-new-revenue rate, meaning the rate that raises the same revenue as the prior year from properties taxed in both years.

The same release puts operating funds at about $250.1 million, adds a five-year capital plan of roughly $347.8 million, and notes that the fiscal year runs October 1 to September 30. It also says the city's finances swing with the seasons, a pattern that suits an island where hotel and restaurant sales hit $672,706 thousand in 2022, by Census figures.

The city rate is only one slice. Galveston ISD, the county, Galveston College and any special district such as a navigation or drainage district each adopt their own rate. The Galveston Central Appraisal District lists every unit that taxes a given parcel on its property page, and the Texas.gov property tax database shows proposed and adopted rates during late summer.

sections.h2: What is the Galveston payment deadline, and how do late fees build up?
sections.html:
Statements are mailed in October, and the bill must be paid by the end of January. Taxes still unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, and the county tax office points out that a postmark after January 31 triggers penalties unless you use one of the payment plans below.

On February 1 Texas tacks on 6 percent in penalty and 1 percent in interest. The penalty then climbs a point per month until July 1, when it stands at 12 percent, and interest keeps accruing every month without a ceiling. A collection attorney hired by the unit may add another charge, capped at 20 percent. A written waiver request goes to the county's Penalty and Interest Committee, and the state allows waivers in limited cases if the owner pays within 21 days of finding out the tax is delinquent.

Galveston County Tax Office payment choices
ChoiceRule as the county prints itSource
Single paymentDue by January 31, delinquent February 1County tax office
Split paymentFirst half by November 30, second half by June 30Same page
Quarterly installmentsFour equal payments, due at the end of January, March, May and July, for homesteads of seniors, disabled persons, disabled veterans and their spousesSame page
Payment agreementCall to set one up; it can head off attorney fees added July 1Same page
Advance paymentPay early and write ESCROW in the subject line with the account numberSame page

Paying online by e-check or card costs a fee. You can also pay by phone at 1-800-420-1663 or leave a payment in the yellow drop box at any full-time office. Payments by mail should use the 722 21st Street address, because the county warns that the postal service does not always recognize the Moody Avenue address.

sections.h2: How can a Galveston homeowner lower the tax bill?
sections.html:
Start with the homestead exemption, which the appraisal district offers to owners who occupy the house. Apply by mail, online or in person, and expect a decision within 90 days of receipt. The general filing deadline is before May 1.

  • The school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and a homeowner who is over 65 or has a disability gets $60,000 more off the school tax base.
  • A local percentage exemption is optional, topping out at 20 percent of value with a floor of $5,000.
  • Seniors and disabled owners receive a school tax ceiling that can move with them to another Texas homestead, and a spouse who survives at 55 or older can keep it.
  • Disabled veterans may qualify for exemptions that scale with the VA rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total homestead exemption.

After the exemption is in place, a homestead's appraised value is limited to a 10 percent annual increase. A value protest is due May 15 unless the notice arrived late, in which case you get 30 days from delivery. The county tax office also lists a tax deferral affidavit (state form 50-126) among its forms for owners who qualify.

sections.h2: How do Galveston's housing numbers read in the Census?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a city that has held steady in size: 53,636 people in the July 2025 estimate against 53,695 in the 2020 count, on 41.05 square miles of land. An owner lives in 46.2 percent of housing units, which leaves most of them to renters.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $326,000, the middle monthly rent is $1,298, and household income sits at $55,631 (2020 to 2024 survey). Roughly one resident in five, 20.9 percent, is 65 or older, and that age group is the one eligible for the school tax ceiling and quarterly installments.

There are 25,198 households of about 1.98 people each. Workers spend 20.2 minutes on average getting to work,, and the Census counts 2,982 veterans living in the city.

sections.h2: How do unpaid taxes affect selling a house in Galveston?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the house into a sale. Each January 1 a lien secures that year's tax on the parcel, and whoever owned it that day stays liable after any later transfer.

Ask the Galveston County Tax Office for a current statement before listing, and check whether a mortgage servicer already paid the bill through escrow. The county explains that a mortgage code only appears after a lender requests the statement, and it suggests signing up for e-statements in the first year after a payoff or refinance so the bill is not missed.

  • On closing day the title company usually subtracts back taxes, penalties and interest from the seller's check.
  • Someone buying after New Year's Day can still claim the homestead exemption for part of that year when the seller never held it.
  • An owner who cannot cover the bill may ask about a payment agreement, available after February 1, before deciding to sell.

Owing back taxes, needing storm repairs or having tenants in place need not block an as-is sale to an investor. Obtain the payoff figure in writing first, so the closing statement shows the tax paid and the lien cleared.

faqs.q: Where does the money go when I pay tax on a Galveston house?
faqs.a: The Galveston County Tax Office gathers payment for the city, Galveston ISD, the county and several other units on a single statement, then passes each unit its share. Statements arrive in October.

faqs.q: What is the tax rate adopted by the City of Galveston for 2026?
faqs.a: The city's figure is $0.416273 per $100 of value, set along with the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. School, county and special district rates are added to reach your total.

faqs.q: Can I split my Galveston property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying half by November 30 leaves the second half open until June 30, with no penalty or interest. Senior, disabled and disabled-veteran homesteads can choose four installments instead, due at the end of January, March, May and July.

faqs.q: By what date should a Galveston owner apply for the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File with the appraisal district ahead of May 1 for the year you want it. The district acts on an application within 90 days of receiving it and will tell you if you do not qualify.

faqs.q: Does a sale make a tax lien on my Galveston house disappear?
faqs.a: No. The lien stays on the parcel until the balance is cleared. The title company settles it out of the seller's funds, so request a payoff statement from the county tax office first.
